paragraphs: Posted by Lily. Teacher Kim asked the Explorers a new question this week. "Should our school library have a music corner for children who study?" Everybody gave an opinion, and here are four of them.

My opinion comes first: I think that the answer is yes, because soft music helps my feelings. Many people think that music makes a person tired, but I do not agree. When I listen to quiet jazz, I feel calm, and I can think. I play it at a low level. It is never a problem for me. Jazz is my favorite kind of music. Last week, I studied for a test with jazz, and I finished my work early.

Mia says, "I think that jazz is perfect, because it has no words." "When a song has words, I listen to the words and not to my book." "Jazz is slow and soft." "When I study with jazz, I read faster." Mia studies at home with a small radio next to her desk, and she writes her stories there. "My kitten Snow likes it too, except when the music is loud."

Leo says, "I think that we do not need music, because the library is for silence." "I am a person who sings when I hear a song." "Then I forget my work, and everybody looks at me." "I like music a lot, and I even sing in the shower." "But I cannot work with it." "Everybody can use the music corner, except me."

May says, "I think that the music corner is a good idea, but not next to the sink." "Children wash their brushes at the sink after art." "The water makes a loud noise." "The corner by the window is better, because it is far from the water." "There the music can be soft." "The readers can still hear it, and I like jazz too."

Teacher Kim read the four opinions and listened to each reason. She smiled at the Explorers. "A person who studies in a library needs a calm place," she said. "I like all four ideas." "Let us try a music corner for two weeks by the window." "The children who like music can use headphones." "The others can stay in the quiet part." "Finally, we will ask everybody what they think." The Explorers clapped for the plan.
